# What was the most valuable pick last year

I wanted to find out which fantasy football players **delivered the most value** in last season’s draft. Using data from ESPN’s Fantasy API and draft results from my league, I analyzed who truly lived up to their draft slot – and who didn’t.

---

## How I Got the Data

I pulled the full draft order, fantasy points scored across the season, and positional ranks for every drafted player. Using that, I calculated a custom version of **Value Over Replacement Player (VORP)** based on our league format:

- 14 teams
- 2 RB, 2 WR, 1 TE, 1 Flex (WR/RB/TE), 1 QB, 1 Kicker, 1 D/ST

VORP was calculated by comparing each drafted player’s points to the **average performance of a replacement-level starter at that position.**

## Overdrafted Players

These players were selected early but returned **below-replacement performance**. In other words, they cost more than they delivered.

---

## Conclusion

This analysis reveals that fantasy value isn’t just about total points. **Drafting players who outperform their positional average** can give your team a serious edge.

Key Takeaways:
- Late-round hits can carry your team
- Don’t overpay for names without checking upside
- VORP helps normalize performance across positions

This kind of analysis can make you a smarter fantasy drafter next season.
